newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-WEIR RECOVERS FROM SHAKY START TO SHARE LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WEIR RECOVERS FROM SHAKY START TO SHARE LEAD.

text.p: Canadian Mike Weir recovered from a shaky start to fire a succession of birdies for a share of the first round lead in the German Open on Thursday.
A closing hole bogey denied the 27-year-old from Ontario the outright lead, leaving him on 65, six under par, alongside Spain's Ignacio Garrido, Dutchman Rolf Muntz and Van Phillips of England.
They were one shot clear of England's Stuart Cage and Jim Payne and Alex Cejka of Germany.
Weir, playing in only his second European Tour event, ran up six birdies and an eagle in seven holes after beginning his round with a bogey and double bogey.
"I'm playing well and brought my game here," said Weir, who won a Canadian Tour event at Mayfair Lakes in British Columbia two weeks ago.
"I kept my cool after the bad start and got on a roll. It was disappointing to spoil things at the end, although I did well to make only bogey. It's a tough hole."
Defending champion Ian Woosnam battled on the new-look course, which was redesigned following criticisms by European Tour officials that it was too easy.
The Welshman was six off the pace and the course's co-designer Bernhard Langer, looking for his sixth national open success, was five behind the leaders.
Langer was forced to wade into the lake to play a shot at the 18th, his ninth hole, but birdied four of his last seven holes to finish at one under.
Woosnam finished at 20-under in last year's weather-affected tournament which was played over 54 holes.
